newsitem.title: USA: Lifeway demand strong, new plant to open.
newsitem.headline: Lifeway demand strong, new plant to open.

text.p: Lifeway Foods Inc said Tuesday strong demand for its products pushed the company to accelerate preparations at its new plant.

"We are continuing to experience a very strong demand for all of our proprietary products, that is taxing our current capacity," Michael Smolyansky, president and chief executive, said in a statement.
The new facility, with more than $50 million sales capacity, will help alleviate current capacity restraints and allow the company to offer new products.

"We expect to begin producing some products in the new plant by July 1, and based on the results of the first quarter, we look forward to 1997 being our fifth consecutive year of record results for Lifeway Foods," Smolyansky said.
Last October, Lifeway bought a 46,000 square-foot building for $1.3 million.
Lifeway is a supplier of the fermented dairy beverage kefir, drinkable yogurts and farmer cheese. It plans to launch a fat-free cream cheese substitute later this year.
